newsitem.title: USA: Apple South to post charge from Hardee's.
newsitem.headline: Apple South to post charge from Hardee's.

text.p: Apple South Inc said on Tuesday it will post an after-tax $375,000 fourth quarter charge from the sale of its 10 Hardee's fast-food restaurants to KEBM Enterprises Inc.
Apple South said the company is selling its Hardee's division for $600,000 less than its current carrying value.
The contract has no significant contingencies and the transaction is expected to close by the end of the first quarter of 1997, Apple South said.
Apple South, which purchased the franchise rights and Hardee's fast-food restaurants in northern and central Florida in 1986, has not expanded its fast food operations in the past 10 years.

The company took a $1.3 million charge in the first quarter of 1996 when the company first announced the decision to sell the Hardee's chain to reflect the accounting rules for the impairment or disposal of long lived assets.
The Hardee's contribution to sales totaled less than two percent for 1996 and an "insignificant amount" of operating cash flow, Apple South said. The company plans to report 1996 results on Monday.
In 1995, Hardee's accounted for $8 million of Apple South's total $440 million in sales.
Apple South currently operates a total of 309 casual dining restaurants in addition to the 10 Hardee's restaurants.
